page: Microsoft Azure FX64mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 64 vCPUs, derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 1344.0 GB of system memory, providing 21.0 GB of RAM per core. It also includes 3780 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the FX64mds_v2 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory throughput. Large-block memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations rank in the top 10% tier, reaching 392.4 GB/sec and 170.98 GB/sec respectively. The server also excels in database operations and static web serving throughput, both scoring in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and cryptographic operations consistently place in the top 25% tier. Single-core performance and text processing are also highly competitive, while LLM inference benchmarks show strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium models.

Given its massive memory capacity and high-frequency dedicated Intel processor, the FX64mds_v2 offers high resource density for memory-bound enterprise applications. The combination of high-speed local storage and exceptional memory bandwidth makes it highly cost-efficient for large-scale database hosting, in-memory caching, and complex data processing pipelines. It is particularly well-suited for heavy database operations, high-throughput web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads that require high CPU clock speeds without GPU acceleration.
